query: What exact experiments will quantify synthetic data limits for long-tail cases (caps on synthetic ratio), and how will we validate synthetic cases do not distort clinical distributions?

response.query: What exact experiments will quantify synthetic data limits for long-tail cases (caps on synthetic ratio), and how will we validate synthetic cases do not distort clinical distributions?
response.answer: Experiments will use synthetic data to simulate long-tail cases, employing statistical tests to ensure synthetic data matches clinical distributions without distortion. Validation will involve comparing synthetic and real data distributions using metrics like KL divergence and accuracy on clinical outcomes.
